_scope.grant_scope: not a grant row: the distance_envelope (buildings, roads) flown on a rail
_scope.cadence: on demand (WP1-07, the distance_envelope on a rail)
_scope.grant_sim_speedup: 1.0 on the hil rail - NOT met headless (measured speedup >> 1)

flight_length.cap: the scenario's max_s + the Loiter operator timeout (30 s) + 5 s

_scope.kpi_bearing_this_run_why: judged per run by guardrail.manifest.is_kpi_grade on the node's manifest

_distinct_kpi_signatures.note: episodes whose KPI tables differ (status, escapes, repairs, breaches, fail-safe, outcome, goal, time to safe, true-state distance and ticks, speed, range, offset). An upper bound on behavioural variety: float jitter in repair counts splits symmetric copies

_seeds.note: a deterministic episode repeated on another seed is identical by construction, not spread

warnings: no episode expects a fail-safe: a Shield whose fail-safe never fires scores the same as this one, so the target is not judged (meets_target None)

_failsafe_labels.observed_as: the escalation FSM entering RTL or Land (Shield.filter's FSM; a Brake or a Loiter is not a fail-safe trigger)

_true_state.basis: true position, harness oracle Shield; the grant's KPI is the Shield's own count (p0_escape_rate), reported unchanged. The autopilot_* figures are the modelled LOITER / RTL / LAND's, outside the Shield's escape rate by definition

vacuous_zeros.false_trigger_rate: structurally 0: the escalation FSM leaves Normal only on an enforced violation (guardrail/fsm.py EscalationFSM._decide) and a row's violations are its input, so no violation-free tick can trigger; the grant's false triggers are the labelled episodes' (failsafe_labelled_episodes.false_triggers)

results.why: A goto pilot flies north up a lane at 4 m/s and 15 m, from x = -20 to x = 70, past one building and one stretch of road of the declared world experiments/worlds/de_block.yaml (policies/distance_envelope_sitl.yaml: buildings 5 m P0, roads 3 m P1, the 10-20 m band, 4 m/s). lane_y -1 passes 3 m from the building's west face (y = 2), inside the buildings envelope; lane_y -11 passes 1 m from the road's east edge (y = -12), inside the roads envelope. The pilot never asks to keep away: the Shield must hold the aircraft out of each envelope while it passes and let it back onto the lane after. The gates are the requirement: no P0 escape, the target reached and the flight ended safe. Not swept: lane 0 (2 m from the face). Measured headless on 2026-11-17 (seed 1001, ideal vehicle) the goto pilot, aiming back at y = 0 the whole way, keeps pressing into the envelope after the Shield has pushed the aircraft to y = -3.2, and the FSM holds it in Loiter at x = 16.3 from 10.4 s to the end: a safe hold, not a pass, and a different scenario (a pilot that presses), which this family is not. ON THE RIG'S VEHICLE the family is not yet shown to hold: on the headless comparison arm (--response-arms ideal rail --autopilot-hold in_place, the hil rig's fitted response, 2026-11-17, seed 1001) both cells count one breach - the aircraft is carried into the rounded corner of the envelope where it begins (lane -1 at x = 15.9, lane -11 at x = 7.3), the commanded forecast not modelling the vehicle's lag (the own-velocity forecast is off on the rails) - and lane -11 ends in RTL short of its target. A likely mechanism, not yet measured in flight: the clearance forecast looks only dt + v / (2 x 3 m/s^2) ahead (Shield._clear_horizon_s: 0.1 + 4/6 = about 0.77 s at 4 m/s), against the rig's lag. The labels below are the requirement and stay as written whatever the hil flights show: a cell that fails there is pinned under known_failures with its measured mechanism and the gates it fails (experiments/scenarios.yaml, "Gates hold the REQUIREMENT"), never re-labelled to the outcome.
